gen-gf-warnes-gf-noto-sans-malayalam: Expressive and widely spaced, Warnes tapers its strokes off before they touch; Noto Sans Malayalam keeps a dense, middle-heavy line. Give the body text a little extra size to open it up.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-noto-sans-mandaic: Warnes draws tube-like strokes that resemble neon glass, spaced wide, while Noto Sans Mandaic has lowercase rising close to the capitals. Let the body text go a touch larger than usual.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-noto-sans-myanmar: Bold letters, stretched wide, with an outline you could trace with a finger. Made small, Warnes would lose that traceable line, while a large Noto Sans Myanmar would only thicken its heavy-looking strip of text.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-noto-sans-nandinagari: Warnes tapers its ink strokes off before they touch, and its r, n and m have arches matching their stems. Noto Sans Nandinagari stays friendly across paragraphs, with generous openings and short ascenders.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-noto-sans-old-hungarian: Spacious, stretched, and bold: Warnes keeps its thickness steady around curves. Noto Sans Old Hungarian has large open counters, and its apertures stay open at tiny sizes, so body text can go small.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-noto-sans-old-permic: Warnes goes for display drama, with spaced-out strokes and no pinching at the curves. Noto Sans Old Permic handles the quieter work, with rounded open forms and lowercase nearly as tall as the capitals.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-noto-sans-old-turkic: Chunky, tall lowercase and open-mouthed curves make the body text easy going. Noto Sans Old Turkic stays clear beneath Warnes, whose pipe-cleaner strokes give the pair its bold edge.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-noto-sans-oriya: Contemporary and bold, Warnes looks drawn with a single nib. Noto Sans Oriya, with generous curve gaps and small letters nearly capital height, gives the spaced-out heading a sturdy partner.
